title: Left derived values invert the multiplicative system
statement: In Situation 05S8 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], let $s:X\to Y$ be a morphism in $S$. Then $LF$ is defined at $X$ if and only if it is defined at $Y$, and in this case the map $LF(s):LF(X)\to LF(Y)$ between values [lem-pur-derived-functor-morphisms-05sa] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Install the right fraction calculus supplied by Situation 05S8. Construct S/X as a cofiltered category: the identity denominator proves nonemptiness, MS2 completes a pair of denominators to a common source, and MS3 equalizes parallel arrows after a denominator refinement. For s in S construct c:S/X→S/Y by postcomposition. MS2 gives an arrow c(a)→b for each b in S/Y. For parallel arrows c(a)→b, MS3 applied to b.hom gives a refinement of a equalizing them. Mathlib Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered proves c initial. The composite of c with the denominator diagram over Y is definitionally the denominator diagram over X. Apply initial_iff_essentiallyConstantProDiagram to obtain equivalence of essential constancy with each fixed value L; existentially quantify L to obtain the iff of definedness.

source.place: Lemma 05SB(2), using Situation 05S8 MS1-MS3 and Categories Lemma 0A1T

proof.text: For the supplied cone uX, prove the limit property explicitly: if j₀ and r witness essential constancy, lift a cone v by v(j₀) composed with r. At each j the common-stage factorization and naturality of v give the leg equation; the retraction equation at j₀ gives uniqueness. Apply the same construction to uY. Mathlib Functor.Initial.isLimitWhiskerEquiv restricts the uY limit along c. The two limit cones over S/X have a canonical conePointUniqueUpToIso e:LX≅LY. Its hom satisfies e.hom composed with uY(c(a)) = uX(a). Every denominator square gives an actual arrow c(a)→b, so naturality of uY supplies the required first equation for e.hom. Applying F to the denominator square, using functoriality and this first equation gives the outer rectangle. The hom of e is an isomorphism. This constructs the comparison directly, without invoking 05SA or leaving a separately chosen inverse.
